additional_info.subject: RE: ID0465743-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP/RD170003091] Plc and power converter fault CRM:03056000687
additional_info.body:
Ciao Giovanni,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0465743
for the Sicharge D at CLIVET customer.
I discussed the topic yesterday with Giuseppe. The issue is that the charger has no communication with the dispenser. I checked on AWS, and it seems the dispenser was never communicating with the charger for the past month.
The error flags that you see are a consequence of this missed communication. The charger can group the converters for the first two converter groups, but because a dispenser is connected and it is not communicating, it cannot group the other two groups.
I checked yesterday with Giuseppe, and via SSH the charger cannot ping the PLC of the dispenser and the EcoGs of the dispenser. For these reason, you see all these error flags.
The outlets of the charger are anyway available.
It is necessary to go onsite and verify the Ethernet connection between the charger and dispenser, and the 7-signal cable between the two of them. I attach the dispenser manual for your convenience.
Please let me know in advance if you need support on the day of the activity, so I can make myself available for support.
I will transfer this ticket to the
eMobility RC-IT SI E Queue.
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: 0465743 - ID0465743-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP/RD170003091] Converter_Group_DC3&DC4 No active converters found CRM:00314000247
additional_info.body:
Ciao Giuseppe,
I am writing you a summary form today's remote support for the charger and dispenser at CLIVET:
We verified that the communication and connections between dispenser and charger were properly done.
Dispenser was off due to blinking fuses FC212, FC213, FC214.
After some tests, we managed to have the changer and dispenser configured. After 1 minute, DC4 went OoO, due to loss of communication with  EcoG KF212.
We performed several tests on the fuses, by adding and removing load, and it seemed that by putting KF211 and KF212 (ecoGs) under fuse FC214, the charger could configure.
At the power-on phase, however, all fuses kept blinking repeatedly , off, on, and red. The 24V DC power supply toggled between 0-6V and 24V.
I believe here we are facing one or more issues at the same time:
One or both ecoGs are damaged and have an abnormal absorbtion.
The DC power supply TB210 is not working properly. IF the fault would have been only on one component being in short-circuit, the fuse upwards would only turn red, without influencing and turning on and off the other fuses.
Please proceed to order the spare parts and go onsite for repair. I believe it would be necessary to have:
#1 24V DC power supply:
#2 EcoGs LE:
#1 fuse 6A (if possible, just in case):
Please let us know when you plan to go onsite and if you need remote support, so that we can schedule the activity in advance.
Thank you again for the support and collaboration!
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei

Hello,
After the substitution of the DC power supply and an inversione of the BC3 and BC4, now the charger is operative.
Therefore the ECOG and fuses weren't substituted.
Kind regards.
